c.tagline: A tiny fortress capital of UNESCO ramparts, deep green valleys, and free public transport for all.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered but relatively expensive and cannot always be hailed on the street; book by phone or via the Webtaxi app. Uber's presence is very limited, so local taxis are the norm.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number for ambulance and fire; 113 reaches the police directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The Gare (train station) quarter can feel seedy late at night with some drug activity and petty theft.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed upper old town on the plateau, ringed by the ancient fortifications and the Bock Casemates, with Place d'Armes, the Grand Ducal Palace, the cathedral and the main shopping streets; the walkable heart for first-time visitors.

The picturesque lower town in the Alzette valley beneath the cliffs, a bohemian tangle of cobbled lanes, stone houses and riverside cafes; its neighbour Clausen adds a buzzing strip of bars and the Rives de Clausen nightlife quarter.

The busy district around the central railway station, with grand boulevards, shops, restaurants and the city's better-value hotels; a practical, well-connected base a short walk or tram ride from the old town.

The modern plateau across the Red Bridge, home to the EU institutions, banks, the Philharmonie concert hall and the Mudam contemporary-art museum; sleek towers and business hotels, quiet in the evenings.
A calm, green, upmarket residential district just west of the centre with parks like Parc de Merl and leafy streets; suits travellers wanting a peaceful stay away from the crowds.

water.note: Tap water is safe and high quality throughout the country.

transit.pay: All public transport in Luxembourg - the Luxtram, AVL and RGTR buses, and CFL trains - has been completely free nationwide since 2020, with no ticket needed for standard (2nd-class) travel; you simply board.
transit.hours: The tram runs roughly 5:30am to around 1am (later on weekends); buses run into the late evening with CN night buses on Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.note: Luxembourg was the first country in the world to make all public transport free; the single Luxtram line links the airport, Kirchberg, the central station and the city centre.

transit.m: Luxtram (free) from Luxembourg Airport to Hamilius in the centre, ~25 min
Bus 16 or 29 (free) to the city centre and station

tip.r: service included; round up for good service

landmarks: Adolphe Bridge
Luxembourg City's grand stone-arch bridge and unofficial national symbol, spanning the Pétrusse Valley with a dramatic single arch.
Notre-Dame Cathedral
An elegant late-Gothic cathedral with distinctive twin spires, serving as the spiritual heart of the city and burial place of the Grand Ducal family.
Grand Ducal Palace
The ornate Renaissance-style official residence of Luxembourg's Grand Duke, guarded by ceremonial sentries in the heart of the Old Town.
Bock Casemates
A UNESCO-listed labyrinth of rock-hewn defensive tunnels carved into the cliffs, offering a fascinating look at the city's fortress past and sweeping valley views.
Chemin de la Corniche
Often called "Europe's most beautiful balcony," this scenic clifftop promenade delivers postcard views over the Alzette Valley and the Grund quarter below.
Place Guillaume II
The lively main square of the Old Town, anchored by an equestrian statue of Grand Duke William II and framed by the City Hall.
Gëlle Fra (Monument of Remembrance)
A gleaming gold-leaf angel statue honoring Luxembourg's WWI volunteers, standing as one of the country's most recognizable war memorials.
Grund
A picturesque riverside quarter of cobbled lanes and old stone houses tucked beneath the fortress walls along the Alzette, best admired from above or along the water.
Neumünster Abbey
A beautifully restored 17th-century abbey in the Grund now serving as a cultural center, its riverside setting making it one of the city's most elegant historic buildings.
Fort Thüngen (Dräi Eechelen)
A reconstructed 18th-century fortress with three distinctive towers, now housing a history museum and offering striking views over the modern Kirchberg skyline.

train.note: Luxembourg's headline fact is that all public transport within the country is free, including trains - you only pay once you cross a border. The TGV reaches Paris in about 2h15 and regional trains cross to Trier in 50 minutes and Metz in an hour. Luxembourg Gare is a 20-minute walk or short tram ride from the old town. Book the TGV early for the cheap fares.

bus.note: Coaches use the stop beside the railway station. Within Luxembourg and on the RGTR cross-border routes into the neighbouring regions, buses are free. FlixBus covers the longer European routes. Carry your passport or EU ID card.

ferry.note: Luxembourg is landlocked with no navigable passenger route - the Moselle forms the German border and carries river cruises that call at Remich and Grevenmacher, but these are excursions rather than transport.

half.name: Vianden
half.blurb: A hilltop castle town in the north of Luxembourg reached by train and bus in under an hour, with a chairlift up to valley views.

half.name: Trier
half.blurb: Germany's oldest city, under an hour from Luxembourg City, with the Porta Nigra Roman gate and ruins of imperial baths.

half.name: Echternach
half.blurb: A medieval abbey town in eastern Luxembourg near the start of the Müllerthal Trail's sandstone rock formations and forest paths.

half.name: Remich
half.blurb: A wine town on the Moselle River in southeastern Luxembourg with riverside promenades and vineyard-covered hillsides open for tastings.
